title: Security Researcher: CJNG's Car Bombs Cluster on Its 'Criminal Frontiers' — Guanajuato, Michoacán, Zacatecas
detail: A September 9, 2026 Infobae analysis of CJNG's car-bomb campaign — anchored on the August 30 Ojocaliente, Zacatecas attack (roughly 200kg of explosives, 11 injured, 10 homes with severe damage, 53 with minor damage, 15 vehicles affected) — cited Universidad Autónoma de Coahuila security researcher Víctor Sánchez Valdés arguing the bombings cluster specifically in what he calls CJNG's 'criminal frontiers': Guanajuato (contested with the Santa Rosa de Lima cartel), Michoacán (bordering Jalisco, contested with local organizations), and Zacatecas (where CJNG holds the south while the Sinaloa-aligned Cabrera family/'La Mayiza' holds the north). Sánchez said car bombs serve to demonstrate capacity, intimidate authorities, and deter local cooperation with rivals, prioritizing social and media impact over casualty maximization, and noted the pressure lands ahead of 2027 gubernatorial elections in the affected states. The piece drew on InSight Crime documentation of the ongoing CJNG–'La Mayiza' dispute involving explosives, drones and land mines, and noted three people have been arrested in the Ojocaliente investigation to date.

confidenceReason: Expert territorial-strategy analysis from a named academic security researcher, published across two related Tier-2 Infobae pieces; the 'criminal frontier' framing is this researcher's interpretive assessment rather than an officially confirmed CJNG strategy.

title: 'El Brilloso,' Alleged CJNG Regional Operator, Arrested in Zapopan — 32nd Detainee in Carlos Manzo Assassination Case
detail: On September 9, 2026, Alexis Jesús Medina García, alias 'El Brilloso,' 31, was arrested in Zapopan, Jalisco, on charges of qualified homicide and qualified injuries tied to the November 1, 2025 assassination of Uruapan, Michoacán mayor Carlos Manzo. Michoacán's Attorney General's Office said Medina García allegedly took part in the encrypted messaging group that coordinated the attack and had assumed leadership of a CJNG-linked criminal cell in Uruapan operating within the 'Los Rs' structure after the November 2025 arrest of Jorge Armando Gómez, alias 'El Licenciado.' Prosecutors also attribute extortion of merchants and avocado producers in Uruapan and Jalisco to him. He is the brother of former boxer Cristian Martín Medina García, alias 'El Vikingo,' detained August 7 and described by prosecutors as maintaining direct communication with 'El R2' of the same CJNG-linked cell. With this arrest, 32 people have been placed before the courts in the Manzo case.

confidenceReason: The arrest and charges are confirmed by Michoacán's Attorney General's Office and corroborated by two independent Tier-2 outlets; Medina García's specific role in the messaging group and cell leadership remain prosecutorial allegations pending judicial determination.
